methods.label: Negate the statement about all shirts
methods.explanation:
For a statement about all objects to be false, at least one object must fail the stated condition. Thus there must be some shirt in this store that is not on sale, which is statement II. Saying this is equivalent to saying that not all shirts are on sale, so IV is also true.

Statements I and III both say that no shirts are on sale. They need not hold: a store with one shirt on sale and another at a non-sale price makes the original statement false while making I and III false. Therefore exactly II and IV must be true, choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary negation of an all-statement and a concrete counterexample.
